_comment: THE ONLY definition of a session analysis. scripts/gen_analysis.py emits, all committed:
Packages/BuilderKit/Sources/BuilderModel/Generated/AnalysisSpec.swift   (Codable wire struct + enums)
mobile/src/generated/analysis.ts                                        (TypeScript types + enums)
server/builder/analysis_spec.py                                         (Pydantic, extra='forbid')
analysis/schema.json                                                    (the JSON Schema handed to `claude -p --json-schema`)
WHAT THIS IS. A model-written reading of one session: what got built, how the person
built it, and how they steered the agent. It is produced ON THE USER'S MACHINE by the
user's own Claude Code (`claude -p`) from a digest of their transcript, and stored
locally. It is uploaded only when `analysis_upload` is enabled (default: on for your
own private view), it is private to the account under RLS, and it leaves the account
only when the session is explicitly shared.
THE HONESTY RULE. Every string field is bounded, every score carries a one-line
rationale, and `confidence` is required. A field the model cannot ground in the
digest is left null/empty, never guessed. Deterministic stats (lines, prompts, tools,
tokens) are NOT in here: they come from the engine and cannot be hallucinated. The
CORPUS numbers (planning ratio, steer rate, code velocity, archetype) are not here
either: analysis/profile.py COMPUTES those, so no model can write them.
SHORT, NOT AN ESSAY. A reading of one session is a headline of at most 70 characters,
a summary of AT MOST TWO SENTENCES, and up to three one-line highlights. The long blocks
nothing ever displayed (features, work_mix, pivots, friction) were REMOVED rather than
left for a model to fill: every field here costs the reader attention.
NO DASHES. No string a person reads may contain an em dash or an en dash: use a comma,
a full stop or a colon. It is repeated in the analyst prompt, and analysis/run.py
rewrites any that survive.
Prior art acknowledged: YC's Paxel scores five dimensions (steering, execution,
engineering, product instinct, planning) and names archetypes. The dimension names are
kept so the numbers mean something to people who have seen a Paxel report; the
scoring is per SESSION here, and a profile is an aggregate of sessions, never a single
run. Unlike Paxel nothing here is sent to a third party for summarisation.

fields.name: analysis_version
fields.doc: == spec version. A retuned prompt is a recompute, not a migration.

fields.name: model
fields.doc: model id that wrote this, as reported by claude -p

fields.name: digest_hash
fields.doc: hash of the digest that was analysed; lets sync skip an unchanged analysis

fields.name: digest_coverage
fields.doc: fraction of the session's events that fit in the digest (1.0 = nothing sampled out)

fields.name: headline
fields.doc: one line: what this session was. Past tense, no trailing period, no dashes.

fields.name: summary
fields.doc: AT MOST 2 sentences: what got done and how it ended. No dashes.

fields.name: highlights
fields.doc: up to 3 one-line highlights, each a concrete thing that happened, with a number where the digest gives one. No dashes.

fields.name: archetype
fields.doc: null when the session is too short to say

fields.name: decision_patterns
fields.doc: signature moves in how the person directed the agent, each grounded in a prompt

fields.name: growth_edge
fields.doc: specific things to try next, grounded in THIS session. One short sentence each, no dashes.

fields.name: confidence
fields.doc: 0-1: how well the digest supported these conclusions

fields.name: contains_sensitive
fields.doc: the model noticed secrets/PII in the digest; the UI warns before sharing

BuildStyle.name: architecture_note
BuildStyle.doc: how they structured the work, if visible. One sentence, no dashes.

DimensionScore.name: rationale
DimensionScore.doc: one line, grounded in the digest. No dashes.

Prompting.name: specificity
Prompting.doc: 0-100: how precisely prompts specified what was wanted

Prompting.name: correction_share
Prompting.doc: fraction of prompts that corrected or redirected the agent

Prompting.name: question_share
Prompting.doc: fraction of prompts that asked rather than directed
